## Design

### 2026-10-10 – Oct 10: Finally decided the project and start designing the PCB, got few ideas too.

**2h**

Oct 10: Finally decided the project and start designing the PCB, got few ideas too.

I will build ESP8266 WIFI AP Controlled Quadruped Robot by  *Musa Wilmar*. I've been wanted to build a actual project features such thing and this Quadruped is actually a real guide to how anyone can build their first Quadruped.

So I decided I shall build this with little of upgrade in hardware such as using a ESP32 instead of two different micro controller, adding a HC‑SR04 to enchant the project with a obstacle avoiding robot feature and using my already present ADXL345 so self  balancing and all.

It's my first time designing a PCB too, wish me luck and suggest me how can I improve the PCB once it's done.

### 2026-10-11 – Oct 12, Done with the basic schematic and the basic BOM

**11h**

Oct 12, Done with the basic schematic and the basic BOM
Today I've been working on the project since morning cause it was Sunday there was almost nothing to do except study and building this project.

First I tried to setup HCSR04 sensor and after checking on the internet I found a page sharing how can we use a ultra sonic sensor with an ESP32. It contains code example, WAKWI diagrams etc. it really helped a lot to understanding the flow easily.

In case anyone interested, here's the page direct link: https://randomnerdtutorials.com/esp32-hc-sr04-ultrasonic-arduino/

![HCSR04](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/2efc76469721ccb31012106559dd58c78952c4df85540d52b7dc038796fbc682.jpg)

![output](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/99f98591c6c1f63137f4586f3ae69cb54691f84a70c7b959c127f6e502f9c049.png)

Fun fact: I tried ultra sonic sensor to actually disrupt a microphone input and it really worked, guess I can't attach audio files otherwise I would definitely share it here.

Afterwards I went to servo with esp32 phase in which I simply tried code example and it was easy and pretty interactive experience.

![sg90](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/9d67dab059d909f54e8daa4157b4b2005a2b4718b77dc26f5947fe799c9b1d31.jpg)

![directservoplay](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/b3345c86737f358ed9dacf3799d533c6ad0e1da512f338cf954998881bbb8168.gif)

  Ignore that tape btw. If you notice that servo isn't moving smoothly that's why I switched to the next phase.

After SG90 and HCSR04 I went for PCA9685 which was really hilarious experience. To start with it I attached a external power source 'a USB cable' to it's green terminals and tried to use it through code examples and Gemini but the it didn't worked and I really tried some great amount of examples.

![faliedPCAtest](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/992e86a458d3f55167f40a0bb059b4dce812620eb8c2153059baa1f3e9a74109.jpg)

Then I tried to test if the external power supply terminals were working or not, so to test that I literally tried to reverse polarize it without knowing what could happen and guess what? **I got to see a little magic smoke out of the capacitor** You can say it was luck that I didn't removed my hand from the USB such that I unplugged it within a second and saved the hardware from becoming a trophy to represent my silliness.

![magicsmokePCA](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/79f500578cfdb7e6b5b4d31ffa4ff9a7c8182b0bfe79db6dc87fa02f22b0c968.jpg)

Afterwords I unplugged all the wires and didn't even used that external power supply cause I have noticed that there's something off with that setup, so I used VIN because there's  only one servo and ESP32 can easily handle it.

![newsetup](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/acf38b548d2dcdc7712ea420fee1fe5d2b753117898a2848e77fbf11b9ca8df2.jpg)

Guess what? It really worked.

![newsetup1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/d6f2be72dfd6daf8c811986d259f579723438fe75542b0b6c7ec8222a740d2da.jpg)

![newsetupppppass](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/2089b867fcd46376832192bd436626142f0a184c584590618383472e5c32fa04.gif)

Did you notice that? The servo is moving pretty smoothly now. The time it starts working I was really **relaxed**.

Now's most basic things is done, I know the right and default GPIO for each so I moved onto the last phase where I actually tired to design a schematic for the PCB.

![schema1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PlE7d7b1gTe9WbvaGUjXHnDcktlvKcOd/94d956256731531541be567f23b7f22776be8d73cf19dc3ca370039772523489.jpg)

**Now I need a little help, if you can notice in the above low quality image that there's two power source, one for high voltage and another one for logical power which only needs 3.3V max so I'm thinking that: Instead of two power supply I should actually add a component that can cut voltage onto the expected ratio. I'll try to check it online tho experienced ones can help in this thing better.**
